title: Write a price file every store can read back

blocks.text: A retail chain writes a price file every night, one `sku;price` line per product, and every store imports it; stores sometimes fix a price by hand and import the file again. Since the nightly job moved to a server in Lyon, no store has been able to import the file. Before that, a hand-edited file once put a product on the tills at a price that no discount rule or price check would touch.
`write` and `read` already handle the lines. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/PriceFile.java`:

items: `formatPrice(price)`: the price with two decimals, the same on every store's server;
`parsePrice(field)`: the price a field holds, or an `IllegalArgumentException` when the field holds no usable price.

cases.says: on a US server the file has two decimals per price and reads back to the same prices
a server whose default locale is French or Austrian writes the same file, with a dot
NaN, Infinity, a comma decimal or an empty field is refused with an IllegalArgumentException

origin.section: Text Conversions: parseInt Rejects Spaces, parseDouble Accepts NaN, and String.format Uses the Default Locale

concepts: String.format without a Locale uses the JVM's default locale, so a number written on one machine may not parse with Double.parseDouble on another; pass Locale.ROOT.
Double.parseDouble trims spaces and accepts NaN and Infinity, while Integer.parseInt rejects spaces; a parsed double is checked with Double.isFinite.
